$comment: Curated mutation targets. Every entry is a piece of logic where a silent
test regression has a real, argued blast radius — NOT a coverage wishlist.
The check only runs an entry when the PR touches its `file` or one of its
`tests`, so an unrelated PR pays nothing.
Adding an entry: name the narrowest `symbols` that cover the logic (an
unscoped entry on a large module is hundreds of mutants), point `tests` at
the scoped suite, and state `why` in terms of what breaks silently.
Run `node scripts/check-mutation-coverage.mjs --all` locally first: a new
entry with surviving mutants fails CI, and the fix is a test that kills
them (or a `// mutation-allow: <reason>` if the survivor is genuinely
equivalent — see src/util/log-rotation.ts:641 for what that looks like).
`mutants` is MANDATORY and is a ratchet, not documentation: the check
hard-errors when enumeration disagrees with it. The operators only visit
`if` statements and multi-arg calls, so a semantics-preserving refactor to
a ternary / `&&` / `switch` / loop guard SHRINKS the mutant set at the same
site and every surviving mutant still dies — a clean pass over logic that
was never perturbed. Measured: tier 2 of `selectEvictionVictim` rewritten
as `findIndex` + `staleIdx >= 0 ? … : …`, with the discriminating test
reverted, went from `4/4` to `2/2 mutants killed — OK` at exit 0. Update
the number only after re-reading the target and confirming the logic is
still covered, in the same commit as the refactor.
ADMISSION CRITERIA — an entry costs more than the diff gate suggests:
1. HERMETIC SUITES ONLY. No docker, no network, no host state, no
wall-clock sleeps. The check runs the scoped suite once per mutant
plus a baseline, so a flake anywhere in it becomes `BASELINE IS RED`
and blocks the merge queue on a lint job that never ran tests before.
2. THE DIFF GATE DOES NOT APPLY ON THE QUEUE PATH. `GITHUB_BASE_REF` is
unset on `push: main` and on `merge_group`, and `changedFiles` in
scripts/mutation/changed-files.mjs treats an unresolvable base as
`run everything`
(as does a shallow checkout, via the same fallback). So EVERY entry
runs on EVERY merge-queue entry and every push to main, not just on
PRs that touch it. Budget the whole manifest at queue time: the one
shipped target is ~7s (4 mutants + baseline x ~1.7s scoped vitest).
3. THE JOB CEILING IS THE REAL BUDGET, AND IT IS THE WORST CASE, NOT THE
TYPICAL ONE. `bun lint` now executes vitest, inside a job with a
`timeout-minutes` (15 in BOTH ci-lint.yml `lint-run` and ci-full.yml
`lint-full` — raise them together). An entry runs `mutants + 1`
suites (baseline included), each bounded by MUTANT_TIMEOUT_MS = 120s
in check-mutation-coverage.mjs, so its worst case is
`(mutants + 1) x 120s` — 10 minutes for the 4-mutant target shipped
here, against a ~7s typical. That worst case is reachable: `force-
true` on a loop guard spins. Before adding an entry, check that
`lint body (~57s) + SUM over entries of (mutants + 1) x 120s` still
fits the ceiling; a second 4-mutant entry does not, and needs the
ceiling raised in the same PR. Overrunning it is fail-closed — the
job dies, the required `lint` context fails, the queue entry is
blocked — but it dies WITHOUT the report naming the mutant that hung.

targets.why: #4663. Victim selection decides whether a synthetic approval outcome — the one inbound class the operator cannot resend, because the Approve tap already happened — is dropped from the pending buffer. Neutralising the tier-2 age bound left all 76 tests green (git show 2338c280); the agent would block forever on a wake-up that is never coming, and nothing in CI would say so.
